# Naming the USD split whose money reached a CAD bank.
#
# The split states 100.00 USD and its own CAD value. The invoice is USD and the
# receivable is USD, so the settlement is what the split already says and no
# rate has to be found — which is exactly what `the_settlement_amount` answers:
# where the split being placed is already in the record's currency it returns
# that split's own figure and never asks the bank.
#
# The refusal beside it disagreed, weighing the *bank's* currency
# unconditionally and turning this away as a conversion nobody wrote a rate
# for. It also said something untrue of this split — "what the split being
# placed carries is the figure that stood in for the receivable, not a
# conversion of it" — when it is a stated conversion.
#
# So the deterministic spelling was strictly weaker than the one the docs call
# optional: `txn_guid:` alone settles this file, and naming the split refused
# it.
#
# What this fixture produces: the split on `Assets:Accounts Receivable USD` at
# −100.00 USD, valued −139.00 CAD, in the invoice's lot.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-04
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank"
    txn_guid: "11223344556677889900aabbccddeeff"
    txn_split_guid: "3344556677889900aabbccddeeff1122"
